prose: Alex Kantrowitz interviews Sundar Pichai, who has little patience for doubts about Google's frontier ambitions: Gemini 4 Argon, he notes, processed three times as many tokens in 72 hours as Gemini 3, and beats OpenAI's and Anthropic's public models on coding, math, science, and knowledge-work benchmarks. Pichai calls frontier research 'ground zero' and says the cloud business is at any moment forgoing short-term revenue to fund the compute trade-offs it requires, pushing back hard on chatter that Google would settle for good-enough Flash models. The conversation also covers AI's role in developing better models, the future AI interface, competition with OpenAI, the Anthropic and Apple partnerships, data centers in space, and the nature of his optimism.
highlights: Pichai: frontier research is 'ground zero'; cloud forgoes short-term revenue for it
Argon processed 3x Gemini 3's tokens in its first 72 hours
Claims Argon beats OpenAI and Anthropic public models on key benchmarks
Rejects the idea Google would settle for lightweight 'Flash' models
Also covered: Anthropic and Apple partnerships, data centers in space, the future interface
Big Technology Podcast interview at Mountain View
